method: Sellke–Berger–Pericchi minimal Bayes factor: BF = 1/(-e·p·ln p) for p < 1/e, else 1; binomial LR for recovery claims; directional claims credit only sign-consistent effects; null claims update with the reciprocal BF (maximal support for the null). Sequential updates multiply odds; same-data re-runs are idempotent (evidence IDs absorb once).

H-BANK.claim: Shrinking the energy bank (capacity 100 → 25) lowers standing population across habitats.
H-BANK.qualitative: The energy bank is the only buffer against an unlucky sequence of metabolic costs; a 4× smaller reservoir converts ordinary cost jitter into die-offs, so colonies lose agents before they can offset losses with births.

H-META.claim: Raising basal metabolism (1.0 → 1.5) shifts standing populations down.
H-META.qualitative: Higher basal charge spends the same income faster: every agent pays more per tick, growth margins shrink, and (at this energy-rich baseline) the cost never converts into extra activity that could pay it back.

H-SUPPLY.claim: Raising food regeneration (supply) raises colony growth.
H-SUPPLY.qualitative: Supply elasticity is live: regen feeds the standing resource pool that populations graze on, so a 10× higher regen should convert into more headcount — the effect is expected to be noisy across habitats because barren windows constrain how much supply can be captured.

absorbed.detail: paired n=4: Δmean=-0.75, t=-3.00, df=3, p=0.058, BF≤1.00 (sign opposes claim → BF=1)

H-FAMINE.claim: Supply destruction (catastrophic food loss) depresses standing population on every habitat.
H-FAMINE.qualitative: Food is the shared public capital: wiping it out at a fixed tick removes the population's only growth margin for the rest of the window, so the standing population after a famine tracks the famine, not the habitat.

H-BOUNTY.claim: A one-shot resource pulse (bounty) raises population when the habitat can absorb it.
H-BOUNTY.qualitative: A pulse is an option, not a floor: it only converts into headcount where the window already supports reproduction; on barren windows the pulse is consumed and forgotten within a few ticks.

H-NUKE-IRRECOVERABLE.claim: A total-cull event is NOT recoverable within 4× the developmental horizon (no recolonization).
H-NUKE-IRRECOVERABLE.qualitative: With no immigration and no founder seed, an empty world has no mechanism to re-seed itself: extinction is absorbing at this horizon because recovery requires births from survivors, and a true cull leaves none.

absorbed.detail: binomial: 0/4 recovered, θ̂=0.17, LR=7.72 → BF=7.72 (vs chance 0.5)

H-METEOR-SURVIVABLE.claim: A spatially-localized impact (meteor at the colony centroid) is survivable — colonies persist.
H-METEOR-SURVIVABLE.qualitative: A localized shock removes agents only inside its radius; the colony's spatial spread and the surviving out-of-radius agents provide both the population floor and the reproduction needed to recover within ticks.

absorbed.detail: binomial: 4/4 recovered, θ̂=0.83, LR=7.72 → BF=7.72 (vs chance 0.5)

H-EARTH-CALIBRATED.claim: Earth-like physics laws are indistinguishable from legacy physics (calibration tie-out, no effect).
H-EARTH-CALIBRATED.qualitative: The engine's legacy climb cost was calibrated to Earth gravity (4.0 ≈ 9.81 × 0.408), so Earth-like law should reproduce legacy dynamics — a null result here is a *calibration confirmation*, not a trivial non-effect.

H-ESCAPE.claim: The escape-window (universe constant) materially changes growth outcomes.
H-ESCAPE.qualitative: The escape radius shapes the fractal iteration texture (hazard/energy terrain) rather than actual escape dynamics at these speeds; changing it re-samples the growth surface, so the sign of the effect can flip by habitat.

H-KLEIN.claim: The klein bottle boundary (non-orientable cap loop) differs from the torus in cap-growth.
H-KLEIN.qualitative: Edge-seeded founders engage the boundary immediately; if the flipped cap-loop reorganises dispersal, Δpop distributions should separate — but between-biome variance is large, so this needs the 17-biome paired panel to even be visible.

H-JULIA.claim: Julia-set terrain outgrows perlin terrain at matched biome/resolution (terrain complexity pays).
H-JULIA.qualitative: Julia windows concentrate resource structure into coherent patches that colonies can exploit, while perlin noise spreads the same resource thinly; the advantage should appear as higher Δpop at matched zoom/resolution.

H-LATTICE-1D.claim: 1D lattices bottleneck colonization relative to 2D (dimensional phase change).
H-LATTICE-1D.qualitative: At fixed volume, a 1D chain has only 2 neighbours per cell: any blockage severs the network, while 2D+ give the colony alternate routes around poor cells — the prediction is a hard phase change between 1D and 2D, not a smooth gradient.
